question: Does a prescribed outer density enhancement retain excited hydrogen and improve the phase-local H-alpha contrast after full native populations, radiation and thermal balance are re-solved?
scope: A spherical radial precursor with an explicitly required supporting force. It is not a magnetic equilibrium or a restricted angular sector.
implementation: Use the native current-T/mu reference wind, multiply rho by q=exp(log(D)*smoothstep((r/Rp-1.3)/0.425)), divide velocity by q, and subtract dlog(q)/dr from the velocity gradient. All native composition and thermal equations and spherical H-alpha transfer are retained.
baseline: The previously accepted spherical H-alpha root at D=1; the original PR13 observer remains a second fixed comparison.

numerical_acceptance.retained_guards: Native transport/species/reference-domain validity; reference Parker convergence only, not modified-flow momentum adequacy.
numerical_acceptance.backend_check: Exact-coordinate CPU evaluation before a final physical/observational assessment; no silent polishing.

diagnostics: Actual density relative to D1 as well as prescribed q relative to the current-T/mu reference wind.
n2, n3/n2, local H-alpha source/opacity, temperature and outer column after full equilibrium.
Radiative heat, thermal advection and expansion including the compression term in the density transition.
Additional support relative to the reference flow and its sampled momentum defect, kept distinct.
Same native complete-band target B[-40,-16), C[-8,8), R[16,40), phases 0.3761495834419293 to 0.3932225607463806, both pixel interleaves and full-data Q.
comparison: Use both fixed original RV/amplitude and the same two profiled nuisance parameters for every candidate. Compare to D1 and PR13; retain all attempted factors and unsuccessful numerical attempts. A selected improvement is descriptive, not calibrated evidence.
limitations: The imposed supporting force is not derived from a magnetic field, pressure boundary or MHD solution; its dissipation is unspecified.
The existing local-SE thermal closure omits advected excitation/ionization energy.
The full H-alpha population group is static CRD with natural/thermal widths; its transfer adequacy and high-density broadening remain separate.
Eight atmospheric cells, fixed lower boundary and the existing continuum/atomic approximations are retained; observer refinement does not qualify atmospheric resolution.
A spherical shell includes halo emission and does not represent partial foreground covering.
